title: Jacob's Wage Agreement with Laban
english: Jacob said, When will I build a house for myself? And Laban replied, What shall I give you? Jacob answered, You will give me nothing at all.

But if you will do this thing for me, I will again tend your flock today and keep watch. Let all your flock pass by today; remove from there every streaked and dark sheep, and every pale lamb, and every white and spotted goat. These shall be my wages, and my integrity will vindicate me tomorrow, for my wage is known before you.
Any animal that is not spotted or white among the goats, nor pale among the lambs, shall be considered mine. Laban agreed and said, Let it be as you have spoken.

That day he ordered the spotted and white male goats, the spotted and white female goats, all that was white among them, and all that was pale among the lambs to be taken out and placed under the care of his sons, putting a three-day journey's distance between them and Jacob.
Jacob then tended the remaining flock of Laban. We must now briefly summarize the scope of the history as we proceed.
He added that the breadth of the history must now be briefly summarized as we proceed.
translator_notes: The Greek in [p4] contains 'ῥῆμα τούτοῦ' preceded by '69.229' which appears to be a folio or section number; it is not translated as it is not part of the narrative.
The text in [p14] ends with 'προσεπε' which is a clear mid-word cut; no completion is attempted.
Several clauses exhibit slightly awkward syntax typical of Hellenistic Greek, but all are translated literally without smoothing.
The phrase 'μὴ ᾖ ῥαντὸν ἢ διάλευκον' in [p8] uses a subjunctive in a relative clause of characteristic, rendered as 'is not' for natural English.

title: Spiritual Inheritance
english: The gifts you gave me from the world were originally yours, and you have given them to me.
This is evident in the fact that God took all the possessions of your father and gave them to me, as it is written, 'God took all the possessions of your father and gave them to me.' (Genesis 31:9)

The noble brides of the Savior willingly promise to follow him, but they claim to have been bought by him from the world, just as he was, for the Emmanuel was ransoming the churches with his own blood.
As a result, they were alienated from their old father, because they have no share or portion with the world, from which they were also called.
Instead, their wealth is the one beyond mind and reason; he himself is their portion and inheritance, their glory and boast, and all that contributes to their brilliance and prosperity.
The world is gloomy towards its own children because of Christ, and it spends its envy in fire, seeing that it will make the whole world under heaven its own and dominate those on earth.
The world's madness is stretched out to him, and it pursues and kills, referring all its actions to the glory of the Savior and the churches under him, and his children, the multitude of believers.
This is unbearable to see, and it is clear that the world is hostile towards them.

As the scripture says, Jacob rose and took his wives and children on camels, and drove all his possessions, and all his baggage, which he had acquired in Mesopotamia, and all that was his, and departed to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan (Genesis 31:17-18).
Meanwhile, Laban had gone to shear his sheep, but in his absence, Rachel stole her father's idols.
Jacob had hidden Laban the Syrian so that he wouldn't report his flight.
Jacob then fled with all his belongings, crossing the river and heading towards Mount Gilead.
On the third day, Laban was informed that Jacob had fled, and he set out in pursuit with his brothers, catching up to him in Mount Gilead after seven days.
During the night, God came to Laban in a dream and warned him, saying, 'Be careful not to speak evil to Jacob' (Genesis 31:24).
When Laban finally caught up to Jacob, he rebuked him severely for fleeing secretly, like a thief, and stealing his daughters and household gods.
Laban asked Jacob, 'Why have you stolen my gods?' (Genesis 31:30), but Jacob was unaware that his wife Rachel had taken them.
Laban said that Jacob had gone away, having desired to return to his father's house, and he couldn't understand why Jacob had felt the need to steal from him.
Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, while Laban set up his brothers in Mount Gilead.

The translation aims to preserve the original word order and meaning, while also providing a natural and literary prose in the author's voice.

title: Salvation through Christ
english: Our salvation comes through Christ, who calls us to this very thing. As the wise one said, speaking as a disciple, there is no other name under heaven given to humans by which we must be saved. This is a truth that Jeremiah also affirms, saying that the Lord will raise up a righteous branch for David, and a king will reign, making judgment and righteousness on the earth. In his days, Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell confidently. The name of this king is Josedeck, which means 'righteousness of God.'

We are justified in Christ, not by our own works of righteousness, but according to his great mercy. This is the message that God and Father has spoken, saying that his righteousness draws near, and his mercy will be revealed. Christ is the embodiment of this mercy and righteousness, and he has come to us. The glorious choir of saints has also called him by this name. The blessed Samuel, famous among prophets, spoke to the people of Israel, saying that he had walked before them from his youth until that day, and: Behold, I, answer me before the Lord and before his Christ; and again: The Lord is witness among you, and his Christ is witness on this day, that you have not found anything in my hand.

The blessed David clearly condemned the foolishness of the Jews and their shameless boldness against Christ, as well as their childish and plotting thoughts. He reproached them, saying: Why did the nations rage and the people plot in vain? The kings of the earth stood and the rulers gathered against the Lord and against his Christ. For the plans of the Jews' ignorance against Christ are truly vain.

For life would not have died, nor would it have been held in the gates of Hades, if it had not been for the one who said to the spirits below: Come out, and to those in darkness: Be revealed. The prophet Jeremiah lamented Jerusalem as sinful, as a murderer of the Lord, as profane, as ungrateful. He said that the Spirit before their face, Christ the Lord, was taken in their corruptions, where they had said: We will live in his shadow among the nations. It is necessary to choose the grace through faith, as a salvation path, for fighting against God leads to perishing. The Creator of all, the only-begotten Word of God, having emptied himself, was anointed.
